newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County board adopts $12.6 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County board adopts $12.6 bln budget.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors late on Tuesday adopted a $12.6 billion budget for fiscal year 1997-1998.
The Board voted 4-to-1 to approve the budget after a heated debate about proposals to raise county salaries, county spokeswoman Judy Hammond said.
The final $12.569 billion budget was raised from the $11.976 billion spending plan proposed in April by Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer.
The final 1997-1998 budget would expand the county's workforce by 329 positions. The budget includes a $9.9 billion general fund, up from $9.4 billion proposed in April.
"Our financial situation is better, but we're still not out of the woods," Hammond said.

The budget does not include pay raises for county workers. County supervisors said they would consider raising salaries after the state's budget has been finalized. Most county employees have not had a raise for three years, and for many groups it has been four and five years.
